title: Integral branch models and finite reconstruction on a qcqs open–closed tree
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$, the condensed ring of continuous functions to normed $E$, or $\Lambda=\Omega^{\mathrm{fin}}$, whose sections on a profinite set are continuous functions to $\Omega$ with image in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\mathcal F=\{E\}$ in the first case and let $\mathcal F$ be all finite subextensions of $\Omega$ in the second. For $F\in\mathcal F$ write $A_F=\mathcal O_F$ with its norm topology. For each scheme $T$, use the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda_T,F_T,A_{F,T}$ on the small pro-étale site, module objects, and ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. Constructibility means finite constant scalar models on a finite constructible locally closed stratification; $D_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ means bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. A lisse module is pro-étale locally free of finite rank. A scheme is qcqs when it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

Let $V$ be qcqs and let $\mathscr T$ be a finite rooted binary tree of locally closed subschemes with root $V$, all vertices qcqs and all branch morphisms quasi-compact. Every internal vertex is partitioned by a quasi-compact open $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ and its complementary closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a vertex $W$ let $e_W^R$ denote the composite from $W$ to $V$ of the exact edge module functors $j_!$ at open edges and $i_*$ at closed edges, with pulled-back coefficient $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Assume that $\Lambda_T$ is flat over $A_{F,T}$ for all vertices $T$ and all fields $F$ used below. Let $M$ be a $\Lambda_V$-module and suppose that for each leaf $W$ one has $F_W\in\mathcal F$, a lisse $A_{F_W,W}$-module $B_W$, and an isomorphism $\Lambda_W\otimes_{A_{F_W,W}}B_W\cong M|_W$ (zero models are allowed).

For each such leaf put $J_W=e_W^{A_{F_W}}B_W$. Then $J_W[0]\in D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,A_{F_W})$ with Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. There is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category
$$\Lambda_V\otimes^L_{A_{F_W,V}}J_W[0]\ \cong\ e_W^\Lambda(M|_W)[0].$$
More generally these edge composites preserve finite scalar-model constructibility and flat module sheaves, and their scalar comparison maps $e_W^\Lambda(\Lambda_W\otimes_{A_{F,W}}B)\cong\Lambda_V\otimes_{A_{F,V}}e_W^{A_F}B$ are isomorphisms for every $A_{F,W}$-module $B$. Finally $M[0]$ is obtained from the finitely many $e_W^\Lambda(M|_W)[0]$ by finitely many distinguished-triangle extensions in $D(\Lambda_V)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Connecting maps are arbitrary $\Lambda_V$-linear maps; no common finite coefficient field for them is asserted.

proof.text: Combine the finite constant-model stratifications on complementary open and closed children using Scheme.Stratification.openClosed. Quasi-compactness of the open immersion transports constructible strata (Tags 09YD and 09YG). Normalized upperStar composition transports their local models. The exact open extension and closed direct image restrict to the input on their supporting child and to zero on the other; the zero module has a rank-zero finite constant model, including on empty schemes. Induction on Path proves branch preservation of constructibility. The implementation reuses the proved private constructibility helpers of CoefficientHeartLisseExtensionConstructible; no Noetherian hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Use normalized monoidal upperStar and the internal relative tensor comparison to test preservation of monomorphisms by tensor on both children. The tensor kernel restricts to zero on both children, hence is zero by the module-object open/closed detection theorem. Right exactness of tensor upgrades this to finite-limit preservation. The existing proved private integralModel_open_closed_flat helper implements this argument for arbitrary condensed coefficients and a quasi-compact open. Iteration gives flatness preservation along Path. A lisse coefficient module becomes locally free for the raw pulled-back coefficient object via freeAt_iff_standard, and the locally-free tensor exactness theorem proves its flatness.

proof.text: For an open edge the specified comparison is the existing canonical openImmersionShriekIso. For a closed edge prove that the specified pushHom is invertible, rather than choosing an unrelated isomorphism. Its open restriction is a map between zero objects by pullIso and openRestrictionPushforwardZero. Its closed restriction becomes the composite of pullIso.inv and extension of the closed counit, after composing with the target counit. The generic iterated-mate identity push_eq_mate_pull_inv and mateEquiv_counit give this equality. Both counits are invertible by abelian closed support; therefore the closed restriction is invertible. Joint reflection of isomorphisms by open and closed upperStar makes pushHom invertible. Induct on Path to obtain invertibility of scalarComparison at every module, without a flatness assumption.

proof.text: A lisse leaf has a finite free constant scalar model. The preceding steps make its branch extension constructible and flat. Apply the existing generic source theorem DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_singleFunctor_obj_of_flat to obtain amplitude [0,0], and hence finite Tor amplitude. Boundedness of a single and constructibility repleteness identify its cohomology, proving bounded constructibility. The existing proved integralModel_flat_derived_single helper identifies total left derived scalar extension of a flat single with ordinary scalar extension in degree zero, using the K-flat single complex and its invertible derived counit. Compose with the canonical branch scalar comparison from the previous step and with the supplied leaf scalarIso. All constructions work for an arbitrary coefficient family; specialize to the singleton finite-field family and to all finite subextensions.

proof.text: Apply condensed open/closed recollement to N in degree zero in D+, and include the first localization triangle into D. Exactness identifies the outer objects with single(j!j*N) and single(i*i*N), and the middle object with single(N), via the generic exactOuterSingleIso and singleFunctor inclusion comparison. Strengthen the induction to allow any exact additive functor F from the current vertex to a fixed root category and any replete object property P containing all leaf branch objects. At a split apply the child inductions to j! followed by F and i* followed by F, map the localization triangle by F.mapDerivedCategory, and combine the two finite extension products using Mathlib extensionProductIter_add. At a leaf use upperStarId and the identity branch. Specializing F to identity and P to the replete collection of leaf branch objects proves the required finite reconstruction. The root case and empty or zero leaves require no exceptions; all connecting maps stay in the fixed coefficient category.
